title: REET 2026 - Rajasthan Teacher Eligibility Test
meta_description: REET 2026 Level 1 (Classes 1–5) & Level 2 (6–8). Lifetime validity. 7,700+ vacancies. No negative marking. 60% to pass.

hero.one_liner: Rajasthan teacher eligibility test - mandatory for government school teaching in Rajasthan. Level 1 (primary) and Level 2 (upper primary).

what_is_it: REET (Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers) conducted by Board of Secondary Education, Rajasthan (BSER) certifies eligibility for government school teaching. Level 1: Classes 1–5 (primary). Level 2: Classes 6–8 (upper primary). One of India's most competitive teacher exams - 30+ lakh applicants annually, larger than many national exams. Passing REET is first gate; subsequent Rajasthan 3rd Grade Teacher recruitment exam determines actual appointment.

REET comprises 150 MCQs in 2.5 hours with NO negative marking - attempt all questions. Syllabus: Child Development & Pedagogy (30 Qs), Language 1 & 2 (60 Qs), Mathematics (30 Qs), EVS/Social Studies (30 Qs). Qualifying marks: 60% for General (90/150), 55% for OBC/SC/ST. Lifetime validity (changed from 3-year limit in 2021) is major advantage - pass once, appear for recruitment exams anytime in future.

For Rajasthan residents, particularly those with teaching aptitude, REET is a direct pathway to secure government job (salary ₹28,000–55,000/month depending on level, plus pension). Teachers command social respect in Rajasthani society. Teaching also allows work-life balance (regular school hours, 2-month summer vacation). Competition is fierce because of these factors - but serious preparation over 4–6 months positions you in successful band (100+ out of 150).

key_details.label: Negative Marking
key_details.value: No negative marking - no penalty for wrong

exam_pattern.description: Single paper, 150 questions, 150 marks, 150 minutes. No negative marking. Pass: 60% (90 marks) for General.

extra_sections.heading: REET Exam Pattern - Level 1 and Level 2 Detailed
content: REET (Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers) is conducted in two levels, and understanding the exact pattern is crucial for focused preparation.

LEVEL 1 (Classes 1-5, Primary Teacher): - Total Questions: 150 MCQs - Total Marks: 150 - Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes - Sections: Child Development & Pedagogy (30 marks), Language 1 - Hindi (30 marks), Language 2 - English/Sanskrit/Urdu/Sindhi/Punjabi/Gujarati (30 marks), Mathematics (30 marks), Environmental Studies (30 marks) - No negative marking - Qualifying marks: 60% (General), 55% (OBC/MBC), 50% (SC/ST)

LEVEL 2 (Classes 6-8, Upper Primary Teacher):
- Total Questions: 150 MCQs
- Total Marks: 150
- Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes
- Sections: Child Development & Pedagogy (30 marks), Language 1 - Hindi (30 marks), Language 2 - English/Sanskrit/Urdu/Sindhi/Punjabi/Gujarati (30 marks), Subject-specific paper - Mathematics & Science OR Social Science (60 marks)
- No negative marking
- Same qualifying percentage as Level 1
IMPORTANT: You can appear for both Level 1 and Level 2 in the same exam cycle. Clearing both levels makes you eligible to teach Classes 1-8, maximizing your job opportunities.
The exam is conducted on separate dates for each level, so there is no scheduling conflict.

extra_sections.heading: REET to Government Teacher - The Complete Selection Process
content: Clearing REET is necessary but NOT sufficient for getting a government teaching job in Rajasthan. REET is an eligibility test that gives you a certificate valid for 3 years (extendable).
The actual recruitment happens through a separate process called Rajasthan 3rd Grade Teacher Recruitment, conducted by the Rajasthan Staff Selection Board (RSSB).
The selection process works as follows.
Step 1: Clear REET with qualifying marks to get the REET certificate.
Step 2: When the state government announces teacher vacancies (typically 20,000-30,000 posts), apply for the 3rd Grade Teacher recruitment.
Step 3: The recruitment merit list is prepared based on a combination of REET score (40% weightage) and academic qualifications (60% weightage based on graduation, B.Ed, M.Ed marks).

The academic qualifications weightage system (called the 'merit formula') considers: 10th marks, 12th marks, graduation marks, B.Ed/D.El.Ed marks, and additional qualifications like M.Ed, NET/SLET, or Ph.D. Each qualification level has a defined maximum score, and the total across all levels determines your academic merit score.

This means that scoring high in REET is important (it contributes 40% to your final merit), but your academic record contributes 60%. Candidates with consistently high academic marks have a significant advantage.
If your academic scores are average, you need an exceptional REET score to compensate.

extra_sections.heading: REET Preparation Strategy - Subject-Wise Tips
content: CHILD DEVELOPMENT AND PEDAGOGY (30 marks): This is common to both levels and covers topics like child growth and development, learning theories (Piaget, Vygotsky, Kohlberg), inclusive education, understanding individual differences, and assessment methods. Study from NCERT Psychology books and Pedagogy by S.P. Gupta.
Focus on understanding concepts rather than rote memorization.

HINDI LANGUAGE (30 marks): Covers grammar (vyakaran), comprehension (apathit gadyansh), poetry interpretation, figures of speech (alankar), and language pedagogy. Practice previous year papers as the pattern is consistent.
Rajasthan Board Hindi textbooks for Classes 6-12 are the best source material.

ENGLISH LANGUAGE (30 marks): Tests reading comprehension, grammar (tenses, voice, narration, prepositions), vocabulary, and language teaching methodology. Focus on basic grammar rules, practice unseen passages daily, and study English pedagogy from NCERT's 'Language Across the Curriculum.'

MATHEMATICS - Level 1 (30 marks): Covers number system, operations, fractions, LCM/HCF, ratio and proportion, percentage, geometry (2D shapes, perimeter, area), data handling, and math pedagogy. Study NCERT Math textbooks for Classes 1-5.
The difficulty level is moderate - concepts are Class 5-8 level but questions test your ability to teach these concepts.

MATHEMATICS - Level 2 (30 marks out of 60): Covers algebraic expressions, linear equations, geometry (triangles, circles, surface area, volume), statistics, probability, and advanced math pedagogy. Study NCERT Math for Classes 6-10.
Focus on understanding concepts deeply enough to explain them to students.

ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES - Level 1 (30 marks): Covers family and friends, food, shelter, water, travel, things we make, and EVS pedagogy. This section heavily emphasizes Rajasthan-specific content - local flora and fauna, desert ecosystem, water conservation methods (johad, talab, tanka), and Rajasthani culture.
Study Rajasthan GK alongside NCERT EVS textbooks.

SOCIAL SCIENCE - Level 2 (30 marks out of 60): Covers Indian history, geography, civics, economics, and social science pedagogy. Special focus on Rajasthan history (Rajput dynasties, Mewar, Marwar, freedom movement in Rajasthan) and geography (Thar Desert, Aravalli Range, rivers, climate).

extra_sections.heading: REET Salary, Benefits, and Career Growth
content: Once selected as a 3rd Grade Teacher in Rajasthan, you are placed at Pay Level 12 (revised) with a basic pay starting at approximately ₹23,700. With Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance (varies by city), and other allowances, the gross salary for a new teacher is approximately ₹30,000-38,000 per month depending on the posting location.

BENEFITS BEYOND SALARY:
- Government accommodation or HRA in lieu
- Medical benefits for self and family
- Pension under NPS (National Pension System)
- Annual increment of 3% of basic pay
- Leave benefits - 10 casual leaves, 30 earned leaves, and up to 20 half-pay leaves per year
- School vacation periods (summer and winter breaks)
- Children's education allowance

CAREER PROGRESSION:
- 3rd Grade Teacher → 2nd Grade Teacher (after passing REET Level 2 or departmental exam + experience)
- 2nd Grade Teacher → 1st Grade Teacher (through RPSC 1st Grade exam)
- 1st Grade Teacher → Headmaster/Principal (through departmental promotion)
- School Inspector/Block Education Officer (through RPSC exam or promotion)

The promotion from 3rd Grade to 2nd Grade typically happens after 8-12 years of service and requires clearing a departmental exam. Moving from teaching to educational administration (Block Education Officer, District Education Officer) is possible through RPSC exams and offers significantly higher pay scales.

extra_sections.heading: Common Mistakes REET Aspirants Make
content: MISTAKE 1 - Ignoring pedagogy: Many candidates focus entirely on subject knowledge and neglect the pedagogy section. But pedagogy carries 30 marks (20% of the total) and is relatively easier to score in once you understand the concepts.
Don't skip it.
MISTAKE 2 - Not practicing previous year papers: REET has a predictable pattern. Questions from previous years are often repeated with minor modifications.
Solve at least the last 5 years' papers to understand the difficulty level and commonly tested topics.

MISTAKE 3 - Over-reliance on coaching material: While coaching institutes provide good notes, they cannot replace NCERT textbooks. The exam tests your understanding of teaching concepts as laid out in NCERT curriculum.
Study NCERTs first, then supplement with coaching material.

MISTAKE 4 - Preparing for only one level: Unless you are very close to the age limit, always prepare for and appear in both Level 1 and Level 2. The additional preparation effort for Level 2 is minimal (only one extra subject), but it doubles your job opportunities.

MISTAKE 5 - Neglecting Rajasthan GK: Environmental Studies (Level 1) and Social Science (Level 2) both contain significant Rajasthan-specific content. Candidates who ignore state-specific topics lose easy marks.
Dedicate at least 2-3 weeks exclusively to Rajasthan GK.

extra_sections.heading: REET Eligibility - Who Can Appear?
content: REET eligibility criteria differ slightly for Level 1 and Level 2. Understanding the exact requirements helps you plan your preparation timeline.

LEVEL 1 (Primary Teacher, Classes 1-5):
- Minimum qualification: Senior Secondary (10+2/12th) with at least 50% marks AND Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed) of 2-year duration, OR Senior Secondary (10+2/12th) with at least 45% marks AND D.El.Ed as per NCTE 2002 norms, OR Senior Secondary (10+2/12th) with at least 50% marks AND 4-year B.El.Ed degree, OR Senior Secondary (10+2/12th) with at least 50% marks AND 2-year D.Ed (Special Education).

LEVEL 2 (Upper Primary Teacher, Classes 6-8):
- Minimum qualification: Graduation with at least 50% marks AND B.Ed degree (2-year course), OR Graduation with 45% marks AND B.Ed as per NCTE norms, OR Senior Secondary with 50% marks AND 4-year B.A.B.Ed/B.Sc.B.Ed integrated degree, OR Graduation with 50% marks AND 1-year B.Ed (Special Education).
AGE LIMIT: Minimum 18 years, Maximum 40 years (General), 45 years (OBC/MBC/EBC), 45 years (SC/ST/SBC/Women/Divyang/Ex-servicemen). Age is calculated as on January 1 of the exam year.

IMPORTANT: Final year students of D.El.Ed/B.Ed can also appear for REET provisionally. However, they must produce the final degree/diploma certificate at the time of 3rd Grade Teacher recruitment document verification.

extra_sections.heading: REET Certificate Validity and Updates
content: The REET certificate was originally valid for 3 years from the date of result declaration. However, the Rajasthan government has repeatedly extended validity periods in the past.
In recent policy updates, the government has considered making REET certificates valid for a lifetime, similar to CTET certificates (which were made lifetime valid in 2021).

Candidates should check the latest notification on the official REET website (reetbser.com or rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in) for the current validity period. If your certificate is expiring and no recruitment has been announced, you may need to appear for the next REET cycle to maintain eligibility.

REET scores are non-transferable - they can only be used for Rajasthan state teacher recruitment. Unlike CTET, which is accepted by KVS, NVS, and central schools, REET is exclusively for Rajasthan government schools.
If you want to teach outside Rajasthan, you will need the respective state TET or CTET qualification.

extra_sections.heading: Best Books and Resources for REET Preparation
content:
CHILD DEVELOPMENT AND PEDAGOGY:
- 'Bal Vikas Evam Shiksha Shastra' by S.P. Gupta (Hindi)
- 'Child Development and Pedagogy' by Disha Publication (English)
- NCERT Psychology textbook for Class 11-12
- Previous year REET/CTET pedagogy questions compiled in book form

HINDI LANGUAGE:
- 'Hindi Bhasha' by Kiran Publication
- NCERT Hindi textbooks for Classes 6-12
- Rajasthan Board Hindi textbooks
- Any standard Hindi grammar book covering Samas, Sandhi, Alankar, Chhand

ENGLISH LANGUAGE:
- Wren & Martin 'High School English Grammar and Composition'
- NCERT English textbooks for Classes 6-10
- Any standard English grammar practice book with MCQs

MATHEMATICS:
- NCERT Math textbooks for Classes 1-10 (depending on level)
- 'Mathematics for REET' by Arihant or Youth Competition Times
- R.S. Aggarwal for practice problems

ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES / SOCIAL SCIENCE:
- NCERT EVS/Social Science textbooks for Classes 3-8
- 'Rajasthan GK' by Rajasthan Chronicle or Lakshya Publication
- 'Rajasthan Ka Itihas' by Ratan Lal Mishra for Rajasthan history

ONLINE RESOURCES:
- Utkarsh Classes YouTube channel (free REET lectures in Hindi)
- BYJU's Exam Prep REET section
- Gradeup (now BYJU's Exam Prep) REET mock tests
- reetbser.com for official syllabus, previous papers, and notifications

extra_sections.heading: REET vs CTET - Key Differences
content: Many teaching aspirants from Rajasthan wonder whether to focus on REET or CTET (Central Teacher Eligibility Test). Here are the key differences that will help you decide.

ACCEPTANCE: REET is accepted only for Rajasthan government school recruitment. CTET is accepted by KVS (Kendriya Vidyalaya), NVS (Navodaya Vidyalaya), DSSSB (Delhi schools), and central government schools across India.
If you want to teach only in Rajasthan, REET is sufficient. If you want options across India, appear for CTET as well.
DIFFICULTY LEVEL: CTET is generally considered slightly more difficult than REET, particularly in the pedagogy and language sections. However, the difference is marginal, and most concepts overlap.
If you prepare well for one, you can clear both with minimal additional preparation.
VALIDITY: CTET certificates are now valid for lifetime. REET certificates have been valid for 3 years, though extensions and lifetime validity are being considered by the Rajasthan government.

RECOMMENDATION: Appear for both REET and CTET. The exam patterns are 80% similar, the additional preparation required is minimal, and having both certificates maximizes your teaching career options across Rajasthan and all of India.

extra_sections.heading: REET Exam Day Tips
content: On exam day, reach the center 60 minutes early to avoid last-minute stress. Carry your admit card, Aadhaar card, two passport photos, a black ballpoint pen, and a transparent water bottle.
Read each question carefully - there is no negative marking in REET, so attempt every single question even if you are unsure. Start with your strongest section to build confidence and momentum.

extra_sections.heading: Rajasthan-Specific GK for REET Prelims
content:
Rajasthan History & Kingdoms

Mewar Kingdom (7th century–1949): Ruled by Ranas/Maharajas (Sisodia clan). Capital: Udaipur (built by Maharaja Udai Singh II, 1559).

Mewar is famous for: Aravalli fort-towns (Chittorgarh - symbol of Rajput valor, besieged multiple times), warrior queens (Rani Padmavati), independence struggle (Maharana Pratap's resistance to Akbar, Battle of Haldighati 1576). Mewar royals were last to join British, maintaining independence longest.
REET Social Studies (L2): Mewar history, Rani Padmavati legends, Maharana Pratap, Udaipur city development.

Geography: Thar Desert & Aravalli Mountains

Thar Desert covers 60% of Rajasthan (world's 17th largest desert). Characteristics: Sandy dunes, sparse vegetation (acacia, khejri trees), extreme temperatures (50°C summer, 5°C winter), low rainfall (<25 cm annually in Jaisalmer).

Aravalli Mountains: Ancient range (1.2 billion years old), runs north-south through Rajasthan, provides water divide, forests, mineral resources (marble, slate, limestone - Rajasthan is marble capital producing 50% of India's marble). Rivers: Sutlej (northwest), Indus (boundary), Luni (internal), Chambal, Banas (tributaries of Yamuna).
EVS (L1) questions: desert animals (camel, lizards), water conservation (stepwells - traditional Rajasthani architecture), agriculture in arid regions (bajra, jowar - millet crops).

Culture: Folk Traditions & Crafts

Rajasthani music: Ghoomar dance (women's circle dance, Udaipur tradition), Kalbelia dance (performed by Kalbelia snake-charmer caste, UNESCO intangible heritage), Gair dance (male group dance). Folk singers: Manganiars (Muslim caste), Langas (hereditary musicians).

Crafts: Blue pottery (Jaipur - intricate designs), Bandhani tie-dye textiles (Jodhpur, Jaisalmer), block printing (Bagru, Ajrakhpur), camel leather, marble carving, miniature painting. Festivals: Teej (monsoon celebration), Pushkar Camel Fair (largest camel market + pilgrimage), Jaisalmer Desert Festival.
Social Studies (L2): Cultural diversity, tradition-modernity balance, artisan welfare, cultural tourism.

Economy: Agriculture in Arid Lands

Despite 60% desert coverage, Rajasthan is agrarian (65% population dependent on agriculture). Major crops: Bajra and jowar (millets, drought-resistant), cotton, oilseeds (mustard, groundnut), spices.
Rajasthan produces 15% of India's mustard (golden reserves if oil reserves fail), 12% of cotton. Pastoral economy: Camel and livestock rearing (goats, sheep) is traditional livelihood.

Mining: Marble (Rajasthan = India's marble store), sandstone (for monuments), salt (from salt lakes). Tourism economy: Jaipur (Pink City), Udaipur (Venice of East), Jodhpur (Blue City), Pushkar (pilgrimage).
EVS (L1): Water conservation in deserts, sustainable agriculture, traditional ecological knowledge (stepwells, tanks for water harvesting).

extra_sections.heading: REET preparation - what actually works
content: Child Development and Pedagogy (30 marks) is common to both levels and is the most scoring section. Focus on Piaget, Vygotsky, Kohlberg theories, learning disabilities, inclusive education, and NCF 2005.
This section is purely theory-based - memorize and practice with previous year papers.

For Level 1, focus on Mathematics and Environmental Studies at Class 1-5 level - questions are simple but tricky. For Level 2, choose either Science-Math or Social Science based on your graduation subject.
Science-Math questions are from Class 6-8 NCERT. Social Science covers History, Geography, Civics, and Economics.

Rajasthan GK is crucial - 30 marks in both levels. Cover Rajasthan history (Rajput kingdoms, freedom movement), geography (Thar desert, Aravalli range, rivers, climate), art and culture (dance forms, forts, festivals), and current affairs.
Use 'Rajasthan Samanya Gyan' by Lakshmi Narayan Nathuramka.

extra_sections.heading: REET qualification doesn't guarantee a job
extra_sections.content:
REET is an eligibility test - passing it makes you eligible to apply for Rajasthan teacher vacancies. Actual recruitment is done through a separate merit-based process (3rd grade teacher recruitment) where your REET score, graduation marks, and B.Ed marks are combined.

REET certificate is valid for 3 years from the result date.

extra_sections.heading: Attempt both Level 1 and Level 2
extra_sections.content:
You can attempt both levels in the same exam cycle (they're held on different dates). This doubles your chances - if you don't make the cutoff for Level 2, you might clear Level 1.

Primary teacher positions (Level 1) often have more vacancies and lower competition than upper primary (Level 2).

extra_sections.text: REET is Rajasthan's golden ticket to government teaching - clearing it with a high score means a permanent position with the Rajasthan government, full pension benefits, and the respect that comes with shaping young minds.

extra_sections.caption: Appear for both levels to maximize your teaching eligibility in Rajasthan
extra_sections.description: REET is mandatory for 3rd grade teacher recruitment in Rajasthan.

preparation_tips: No negative marking = attempt all 150 questions. This is your advantage. Never leave blanks. Even 50-50 guesses give you expected value of 0.5 marks per question (better than 0 for blank). Strategy: (1) Attempt easy questions first (75 questions in 60 min). (2) Medium questions (50 Qs in 40 min). (3) Difficult remaining (25 Qs in 50 min). (4) Final 5 minutes: verify answers.
CTET and REET overlap 80% - if preparing for CTET, appear for REET with minimal extra effort. Add Rajasthan GK (3–4 weeks) and you're ready.

Child Development (30 Qs) is high-weightage - 20% of exam. Topics: Piaget's cognitive development, attachment (Bowlby), emotional intelligence, special needs, inclusive education. These are straightforward if you have studied B.Ed content properly. Score 24+/30 here is achievable with focused revision.

Mock tests from month 2. Take 2–3 full-length mocks per week. Target: 100+/150 (67%) to be safe. Analyze each mock: Which sections took longest? Where did you make silly errors? Which topics are weak?

faqs.question: Is REET lifetime validity really permanent?
faqs.answer:
Yes. As of 2021, REET validity changed to lifetime - no expiry date.

This is huge advantage. Even if you clear REET today but don't get recruited immediately, your REET score remains valid forever.

You can apply for recruitment exams 5, 10, even 20 years later if needed.

faqs.question: Should I target Level 1 or Level 2?
faqs.answer:
Level 2 (₹36,600+ basic) pays significantly more than Level 1 (₹23,700 basic) - ₹13,000/month difference. If you have B.Ed, always target Level 2.

Level 1 is only if you have D.El.Ed but not B.Ed. You can appear for both levels in same exam cycle, so do both.

faqs.question: REET passing guarantee me a job?
faqs.answer:
No. REET is only eligibility gate.

Actual recruitment is through separate Rajasthan 3rd Grade Teacher recruitment exam (conducted by RSMSSB). You must clear both REET (one-time) + Recruitment exam (periodic) to get appointed.

REET score is valid for recruitment exams conducted anytime in future.

faqs.question: What is the REET 2026 exam date?
faqs.answer:
REET 2026 exam date has not been officially announced yet. Check bser.rajasthan.gov.in (Board of Secondary Education Rajasthan) for the latest notification.

Based on previous cycles, the exam is expected in the second half of 2026. Registration typically opens 2-3 months before the exam.

faqs.question: What is the REET passing marks?
faqs.answer:
General category: 60% (90 out of 150 marks). SC/ST/OBC/PwD: 55% (82.5 out of 150, rounded to 83).

These are qualifying marks - you need to score above this to receive the REET certificate. Actual teacher recruitment cutoffs are usually higher than qualifying marks.

faqs.question: Is B.Ed mandatory for REET?
faqs.answer:
For Level 1: D.El.Ed (diploma in elementary education) or B.El.Ed is sufficient. B.Ed is not mandatory.

For Level 2: B.Ed or equivalent is required along with graduation in the relevant subject. Candidates in the final year of B.Ed can also apply provisionally.

syllabus.topics: Content knowledge + pedagogy. Level 1: primary level. Level 2: upper primary level.

study_plan.tasks: REET includes Rajasthan-specific education content. Study CDP theories + Rajasthan education policies, state board curriculum, local pedagogy approaches. Language preparation.
Subject content from NCERT + Rajasthan board textbooks. Previous year papers. Focus on pedagogy questions in every section. Mock tests weekly.
Daily mocks. Revise CDP and pedagogy. Qualifying marks vary by category. No negative marking. Attempt all questions.
